reading.body:
This record is a single OpenStreetMap node in Wieliczka, Poland, tagged as a data center, with no power capacity listed and no confirmed operator.

The only substantive facts are a name, DISKUS Polska, a website, a coordinate near Kraków, and a distance of 13.4 miles to Kraków John Paul II International Airport. The name suggests a Polish IT or storage business, and Kraków is a real technology and outsourcing hub, so a small operator in the area is plausible. But the entry carries no megawatt figure, no operator confirmation, and no business registration check, and the research note states that verification stopped because search quota ran out.

For AI specifically, this tells almost nothing. A data center that matters to AI training or inference is defined by its power draw and its connectivity, and neither is present here. The absence of a megawatt value is not evidence of a small facility, it is evidence of an unmeasured one. A reader should treat this as a location and a name, not as a capacity claim.

What the data does not cover is the part that would make it useful: whether the site exists as a commercial colocation or hosting facility, how much power it can draw, and whether it is connected to anything that serves AI workloads. The nearest-airport distance is the only piece of infrastructure context given, and it speaks to staff and equipment access rather than to compute.
